articles.title: Kingston’s Quiet Rent Revolution
articles.content_excerpt: KINGSTON, N.Y. — On September 1 , John and Gail Bechtold tore open their monthly rent statement, hoping their landlord had finally given in and fixed it. But those same four numbers stared back at them: $ 1 , 700 . It was the 39 th month in a row that Opus Management Group overcharged the Bechtolds by $ 221 . 74 for their apartment in the Dutch Village (or, as Gail calls it, Dump Village) complex in Kingston. According to a state housing agency ruling, Opus owes the Bechtolds, both retirees in their 80 s, well over $ 10 , 000 . articles.title: The Foundations of Turkey’s Peace With the Kurds Are Shaky
articles.author: Ertuğrul Kürkçü
articles.content_excerpt: Turkey’s political scene is moving. The recently passed Framework Law redirects the Kurdish question — the principal fault line in the country’s imagined national unity — from armed confrontation to regulated pacification. This has political consequences far beyond its narrow legal scope. More than bringing one period of the Kurdish conflict to a close, it opens a new phase in Turkey’s class struggles by reshaping the balance between the state, the Kurdish movement, and the political opposition. The August 10 Framework Law — officially the Law on Strengthening National Solidarity and Social Cohesion — is a genuine rupture in Turkey’s handling of the Kurdish conflict. articles.title: The Last Revolutionary Filmmaker
articles.author: William Andrews
articles.content_excerpt: When the French-Swiss film director Jean-Luc Godard died in 2022 at the age of ninety-one, obituaries celebrated both his boundless cinematic inventiveness and the radical politics that shaped his work. To some, his death marked the end of an era of politically committed filmmaking. But in Japan, another artist as equally radical is still, at age eighty-seven, hard at work. In the last four years alone, Masao Adachi has released two movies, both dealing with political militants — including Shinzo Abe’s assassin — and has also worked with other artists, like French filmmakers Éric Baudelaire and Philippe Grandrieux in the early 2010s. articles.title: Treasury Market Volatility Is Capital Disciplining the State
articles.author: Stephen Maher
articles.content_excerpt: Since the 2008 financial crisis, American economic policy has rested on the seemingly unshakable conviction that global markets for US government debt were bulletproof. This fact would supposedly allow the state to run enormous deficits indefinitely, financing massive tax cuts for the wealthy even while military spending approached $1 trillion. The same confidence underpinned the idea that the Federal Reserve possessed virtually unlimited firepower to contain economic crises. Yet in recent weeks, this assumption has begun to look considerably less secure. It turns out that even the American state is subject to the discipline of capital after all. articles.title: Zack Polanski’s Eco-Populism Could Do With More Socialism
articles.author: Chris Saltmarsh
articles.content_excerpt: The Greens were for decades a relatively marginal force in British politics, with only one member of Parliament (MP) and a modest but growing number of local councilors. However, its prospects changed in September 2025 after Zack Polanski was elected party leader on an eco-populist platform. This new leadership defined itself against Labour Prime Minister Keir Starmer, rejecting his apologia for Israel’s genocide in Gaza as well as his fiscal austerity, anti-migrant measures, and anti-protest authoritarianism. Over the last year, the membership of the Green Party of England and Wales (there is a separate Scottish party) has surged from around 66,000 to over 230,000. articles.title: Zach Cregger Made a Resident Evil Movie With Bite
articles.author: Eileen Jones
articles.content_excerpt: Zach Cregger’s horror-comedy Resident Evil is a real blast of a movie, fast, funny, scary, and inspired. Only an exuberant film lover could come up with such a gleefully inventive ninety-five-minute thrill ride as this one. I gather that Cregger is a fan of the Resident Evil video game franchise. That seems like the only possible explanation for why the acclaimed director of highly praised non-IP horror hits Weapons (2025) and Barbarian (2022), who presumably has a blank check to make any horror-related movie he wants, would choose to make the eighth Resident Evil entry in the twenty-four-year-old franchise. articles.title: German Centrists Are Smearing Die Linke as Antisemites
articles.author: Nimrod Flaschenberg
articles.content_excerpt: Let’s be clear: Die Linke, Germany’s leading left-wing force, which resoundingly won Sunday’s elections in Berlin, is not an antisemitic party. It does not have an “antisemitism problem,” nor is it a menace to Jews in Germany or Berlin. While some Jews in the city perceive the Left as a threat, this perception is fueled by a false media narrative lacking a factual basis.That Die Linke is not a hotbed of antisemitism is obvious to anyone taking an honest look at the party: its leaders, its campaign methods, and the deep, sometimes overcharged embrace of Germany’s anti-antisemitism discourse which governs its rhetoric.
